title: Paths in Maze That Lead to Same Room
summary: A maze with n rooms and corridors connecting some of them is described.
statement: A maze with n rooms and corridors connecting some of them is described. The task is to count the number of unique cycles of length 3 within the maze. A cycle of length 3 is formed when three rooms are interconnected in a triangular pattern. Different cycles are those that do not share all the same rooms.
constraints: Rooms are numbered one through n and corridors are distinct undirected edges.
Count unordered triples in which every pair of rooms has a corridor.
Return the number of distinct triangular cycles.
hints: A triangle is detected at each vertex by an edge between two of its neighbors.
Store neighbor sets, inspect every neighbor pair, and divide the total by three.
For each room and each pair j,k in graph[room], add one if k is in graph[j].
Every triangle contributes at exactly its three vertices and no non-triangle contributes.
editorial: Every triangle contributes at exactly its three vertices and no non-triangle contributes.

tests.explanation: Rooms 1,2,4 and rooms 1,3,4 form the two triangles.
A path contains no three mutually connected rooms.
